body.cap: AJ2 CEO Gil Soo Jung introduces the company’s technology to journalists from five countries—the United States, France, the United Arab Emirates, Taiwan, and Vietnam—at the Global Media Meetup held on Friday, December 12, at MIK Basecamp in Seocho-gu, Seoul. | Photo by AVING News

body.x: AJ2 Co., Ltd. (CEO Gil Soo Jung) participated on Friday, December 12, in the “Global Media Meetup” hosted by AVING News’ International Press Club (IPC) for domestic companies and startups.

AJ2 is a Korean company founded in 2022, drawing on extensive research and development experience and expertise accumulated over many years in iris recognition. Starting in 2024, its third year of operation, the company commercialized security solutions for personal identity authentication and has supplied them across various industrial sites. The company says it continues to generate steady export results with a broad lineup that showcases differentiated functions and technological competitiveness.

These products integrate AJ2’s independently developed hardware, including optical components, with proprietary software, clearly differentiating them from other security solutions. While conventional iris recognition technologies struggled to gain widespread adoption due to stringent recognition requirements and high costs, AJ2 addressed these limitations through AI-based development and design approaches.

Specifically, the company developed its proprietary iris recognition algorithm, named “iris,” by applying CNN deep learning to open-source AI models. It increased recognition accuracy to 95 percent and set licensing costs more competitive than those of conventional general-purpose algorithms, such as facial recognition.

At the same time, AJ2 significantly improved iris image capture accuracy and focal distance by adopting high-resolution lenses and infrared LEDs that effectively suppress light scattering. The company also reduced hardware costs by more than 30 percent compared with competing solutions, enhancing the economic viability of iris recognition technology across both software and hardware.

body.cap: AJ2 CEO Gil Soo Jung introduces the company’s technology to journalists from five countries—the United States, France, the United Arab Emirates, Taiwan, and Vietnam. | Photo by AVING News

body.x: Based on these advancements, AJ2 implemented functionality that rapidly and accurately identifies irises at approximately 1 meter. Through repeated participation in domestic and overseas exhibitions over recent years, the company also conducted successful technology demonstrations of next-generation solutions that extend recognition distance to up to three meters and strengthen resistance to environmental factors such as lighting conditions. As a result, AJ2 continues to expand partnerships across regions, including Japan, the Middle East, and North and Central America.

Building on this momentum, AJ2 plans to return once again to CES 2026, the world’s largest IT and technology exhibition, where it has participated continuously since 2023, to showcase the competitiveness of its technologies and products to the global market and explore new business opportunities.

CEO Gil Soo Jung said, “We aim to highlight the outstanding lightweight design and scalability of our iris recognition technology and move beyond conventional security solutions to open new markets in areas such as mobile biometrics, fintech, and healthcare.”

He added, “The iris serves as a more precise and distinctive indicator than the face or fingerprints, and it also reflects aspects of an individual’s health, making it a powerful biomarker. As a result, the applicability and value of our technology are virtually limitless, and we expect it to strongly attract the interest and attention of global companies across multiple industries.”

body.cap: A view of AJ2’s iris-recognition solution lineup was showcased at the Global Media Meetup. | Photo by AVING News

body.x: Meanwhile, AVING News has introduced Korean companies to the world through partnership cooperation with more than 800 media outlets across 54 countries over the past 22 years. Building on its long-established global media network, AVING News launched the International Press Club in August. Media outlets participating in this Global Media Meetup included Innovation & Tech Today from the United States, Le Café Du Geek from France, Arageek from the United Arab Emirates, and Digitimes from Taiwan.
